Where midwifery sits among 850 specialties

Ranked by each practitioner's first-listed taxonomy — the top 15 nationally, by primary designation. Advanced Practice Midwife ranks 93rd this way (9,767 practitioners list it first), well below the top 15 shown here. Counting it anywhere in a practitioner's qualification list — not just first — is what gets to 15,941, the number used everywhere else on this page: many midwives are coded with a nursing credential listed ahead of their midwifery one.

Cohort match vs. national tag

Two independent ways of arriving at "is this NPI a midwife in NDH" — matching this project's own 16,775 AMCB–NPPES cohort NPIs against NDH, versus scanning NDH nationally for the midwife taxonomy regardless of cohort membership. They mostly agree. The disagreement is the point.

3,237 tagged Advanced Practice Midwife in NDH, found nationally, with no match in this project's AMCB cohort. Not asserted as "midwives AMCB missed" without more work — NDH's taxonomy tagging is payer/PECOS-sourced and can include CMs, inactive NPIs, or the same kind of taxonomy mis-tag NPPES itself carries. It's the full, inspectable list below, not a conclusion.

Source: CMS National Directory of Healthcare Providers and Services, bulk NDJSON release generated 2026-10-14, filtered from 06-Practitioner.ndjson.zst (7,481,907 records) and 07-PractitionerRole.ndjson.zst by NUCC taxonomy code 367A00000X (Advanced Practice Midwife). Full methodology: docs/TECHNICAL_APPENDIX_CMS_NDH.md in the midwifery repo.

Cohort membership = this project's AMCB–NPPES linkage, 16,775 active primary certificants. "Accepting" reflects the acceptingPatients extension on at least one organization affiliation; "Medicare" reflects the cms_medicare_enrollment flag. Absence of either is not evidence of the negative — it means NDH simply has no record either way.
